title: Enquirer’s Guide: Who discovered the first opening?
summary: Later scholars regard an observation by the astronomer Giacomo Maraldi in 1723 as the first accidental opening, though he did not recognize one.
author: The Enquirer’s Guide Desk
paragraphs: This entry from The Enquirer’s Guide answers a question often put to the Society: “Who discovered the first opening?”
Later scholars regard an observation by the astronomer Giacomo Maraldi in 1723 as the first accidental opening, though he did not recognize one.
A reproducible Eidetic aperture was identified during the optical investigations associated with François Arago in 1818. A stable opening large enough for a tethered probe came in 1844.

Readers should treat the answer as an introduction rather than a final authority. Eidetic science in Alderwick is reported through measurements, disputed interpretations and careful revisions, and a respectable enquiry may properly end with further questions.
